Interactive viewing

Source: vignettes/viewer.Rmd
viewer.Rmd

view_3d() opens a plot in an interactive browser widget with orbit controls, tooltips and selection. It uses WebGL 2, the browser graphics API, and the R packages htmlwidgets and svglite to display the scene and its surrounding plot elements. This article builds a viewer and links its selections to a filter. Installation is covered in Get started.

Example

The motor-car data contain weight in thousands of pounds, fuel economy in miles per US gallon, gross horsepower and cylinder count. Model names identify the observations. Map them to the hover text and selection key before creating the widget.

cars <- data.frame(mtcars, model = rownames(mtcars))
p <- ggplot(cars, aes(wt, mpg, z = hp, tooltip = model, data_id = model)) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 4, colour = PAL["blue"]) +
  coord_3d() + labs(x = "weight", y = "mpg", z = "horsepower")

Drag to orbit and use the wheel or a pinch gesture to zoom. Arrow keys orbit, and the plus and minus keys zoom. Camera code copies the current angles into a coordinate call, and Reset restores the initial view.

widget <- view_3d(p, width = 624, height = 432, elementId = "cars-view")
widget

Picking and selection

Picking identifies the primitive under the pointer by its identifier in an offscreen image. Hover over a point to see its model name, then click it to select that key. Shift-click or control-click adds and removes keys; clicking empty space clears the selection. Unselected geometry dims while a selection exists.

Rows sharing a key highlight together across layers. In the absence of a key mapping, each row in each layer receives its own key. The default tooltip lists mapped values. Use tooltip = FALSE to disable those default tooltips; an explicit tooltip mapping still supplies its text.

view_3d(p, selection = "single", width = 624, height = 432)

Set the selection mode to "none" to disable it. In a Shiny application, the widget identifier above gives the selected keys in input[["cars-view_selected"]] and camera updates in input[["cars-view_camera"]]. Browser integrations can listen on the widget element for ggplot3d:hover, ggplot3d:select and ggplot3d:camera events.

Several panels

Facets stay interactive and retain their strips, titles and legends. The example splits the cars by transmission, with zero denoting automatic and one manual. Orbiting either panel turns both by the same amount, retaining their relative camera angles.

panels <- p + facet_wrap(~am, ncol = 1,
  labeller = as_labeller(c("0" = "automatic", "1" = "manual")))
view_3d(panels, width = 624, height = 576, link = TRUE)

Set link = FALSE to move the panel under the pointer alone. An index in panel selects one facet without the surrounding plot elements. The viewers below show automatic and manual cars separately. A shared string links their camera changes on the same page.

view_3d(panels, panel = 1, link = "cars-cameras", width = 624, height = 432)

The second viewer uses the same link name. Orbit, zoom and reset changes travel between the two, with angle changes added and zoom factors multiplied.

other <- panels + coord_3d(azimuth = 30)
#> Coordinate system already present. Adding coord_3d() replaces it.
view_3d(other, panel = 2, link = "cars-cameras", width = 624, height = 432)

Linking data with crosstalk

crosstalk links selections and filters between widgets using shared row keys. Construct the plot from the shared object’s original data and pass that same shared object to the viewer. The cylinder filter below hides cars excluded by the chosen cylinder counts.

shared <- crosstalk::SharedData$new(cars, key = ~model, group = "cars")
linked <- ggplot(shared$origData(), aes(wt, mpg, z = hp, tooltip = model)) +
  geom_point_3d(size = 4, colour = PAL["blue"]) + coord_3d()

The original rows let the viewer take its keys from the shared object. Other crosstalk widgets in the group receive its selections and can send selections back. Keep the plotted rows aligned with the shared data by constructing the plot from that original table.

htmltools::tagList(
  crosstalk::filter_checkbox("cylinders", "Cylinders", shared, ~cyl),
  view_3d(linked, data = shared, width = 624, height = 432))

Saving the widget

Save the widget as HTML to share an interactive view. This example writes the supporting files beside the HTML; distribute the HTML and its companion directory together. Use selfcontained = TRUE for a single HTML file when Pandoc is available.

directory <- tempfile("cars-viewer-")
dir.create(directory)
html <- file.path(directory, "cars.html")
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(widget, html, selfcontained = FALSE)
file.info(html)$size > 0
#> [1] TRUE

Rendering behaviour

Opaque geometry uses a depth buffer. Transparent primitives are sorted by their centre depth, so crossing transparent surfaces can differ from the static vector output. Text is drawn as plain browser text, with a label’s visibility decided at its anchor. Geometry, mapped colours and lighting are transferred once; camera interaction runs in the browser.

Stereo plots use their central camera in the viewer. Static eye pairs and anaglyphs are covered in Camera and framing. Use Documents to switch between an HTML viewer and a static figure from the same knitr or Quarto chunk.
